VERIDANE - INTERNAL - Product Safety Committee memo PSC-2026-07
Date: 2 Oct 2026     From: Elena Kowalczyk, VP Quality & Product Safety     To: Executive Leadership Team

Subject: GV-400 series combination gas valve - voluntary recall (CPSC Fast Track)

Summary
- Affected units: ~41,200 GV-400/GV-410 combination gas valves, date codes 2507-2612, sold to OEMs for commercial rooftop units and unit heaters.
- Issue: diaphragm seat can deform under sustained high-inlet-pressure conditions, allowing gas to pass when the valve is commanded closed. 17 field reports of gas odor; 2 reports of delayed ignition causing cabinet damage; no injuries reported.
- Root cause: change of diaphragm compound supplier (Q1 2025); supplier lot material out of spec on compression set. Corrective action complete; replacement valves shipping from Mequon plant since 28 Sep.
- Regulatory: CPSC Fast Track filed 22 Sep; joint recall notice expected the week of 19 Oct. Canada (Health Canada) notification filed.
- Cost: reserve booked in Q3 $21.6M (field replacement, OEM labour reimbursement, logistics). Range $18-26M. Supplier recovery claim of ~$9M lodged, not recognised.
- Customer impact: three OEMs (incl. our 2nd-largest BCV customer) have paused new GV-400 orders pending the recall notice. Included in updated guidance.

Hartwell Pryce LLP - DRAFT FOR DISCUSSION WITH MANAGEMENT AND AUDIT COMMITTEE - 13 Oct 2026
Proposed Note 2 to the Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements (Form 10-Q, quarter ended 30 Sep 2026)

Note 2 - Liquidity and Going Concern

In accordance with ASC 205-40, Presentation of Financial Statements - Going Concern, management considered whether there are conditions or events, considered in the aggregate, that raise substantial doubt about the Company's ability to continue as a going concern within one year after the date the financial statements are issued.

As of 30 September 2026 the Company was not in compliance with the Consolidated Net Leverage Ratio and Consolidated Interest Coverage Ratio covenants under its Credit Agreement. Absent a waiver or amendment, the lenders may declare all outstanding obligations ($1,176.4 million) immediately due and payable and may terminate revolving commitments. The Company does not currently have sufficient liquidity to repay these obligations if accelerated. The Company has requested a waiver and amendment from its lenders; such waiver has not been obtained as of the date of this draft and there can be no assurance it will be obtained on acceptable terms or at all.

These conditions raise substantial doubt about the Company's ability to continue as a going concern. [Management's plans paragraph - to be provided by the Company. Whether the plans alleviate substantial doubt will be considered at the issuance date.]

Reviewer note (HP engagement partner): if an executed amendment is obtained before the 10-Q issuance date, we will revisit; the note may be reduced to a liquidity disclosure. Until then the draft stands.

# Veridane Fluid Technologies, Inc. (NASDAQ: VRDF) — Q3 FY2026 Letter to Shareholders
### Quarter ended 30 September 2026 | First draft for review by M. Ostrander and D. Whitcombe — NOT FOR RELEASE
### DRAFT 1 of ticket IR-2026-Q3-014 | Release: Thursday 5 November 2026, 4:05 pm ET

Dear Fellow Shareholders,

Data-center momentum led the quarter. Thermal & Data Center Solutions (TDC) grew 13.4% year over year to $156.3 million, we were awarded two new hyperscale cooling programs during the quarter, and our data-center cooling backlog rose 22.0% to $574.2 million. Total backlog ended the quarter at $918.0 million, up 13.0% over the prior-year period.

Those gains were offset by a difficult quarter in core commercial HVAC and by the costs of a voluntary product recall. On a GAAP basis we reported a net loss of $15.6 million, or $(0.37) per diluted share, which includes our GV-400 recall charge and Project Keystone restructuring costs. Adjusted EBITDA was $48.7 million, an 11.8% margin, and adjusted EPS was $0.15. Both adjusted measures exclude the recall charge and restructuring costs, and both are reconciled to the comparable GAAP measures in the table accompanying this letter.

## Highlights
- TDC net sales up 13.4% to $156.3 million, with two new hyperscale awards in the quarter.
- Data-center cooling backlog of $574.2 million, up 22.0% year over year; total backlog $918.0 million, up 13.0%.
- Adjusted EBITDA of $48.7 million (11.8% margin); adjusted EPS of $0.15. GAAP net loss of $15.6 million, or $(0.37) per diluted share, including the GV-400 recall charge and Keystone restructuring costs.
- GV-400 voluntary recall initiated with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) under its Fast Track program: root cause identified, corrective action complete, replacement valves shipping since 28 September.
- Project Keystone launched, targeting $35 million of annualized run-rate cost savings by the end of Q2 FY2027.

## Segment review

**Thermal & Data Center Solutions.** Net sales were $156.3 million, up 13.4% from the prior-year quarter. The CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger ramped with the two hyperscale customers announced last quarter, and we were awarded two additional hyperscale programs during the period. Demand for high-density liquid cooling remained strong through the quarter, reflected in the 22.0% growth in our data-center backlog, which reached a record $574.2 million. Conversion into revenue is phased over the next several quarters, which supports growth into FY2027.

**Building Controls & Valves.** Net sales were $256.3 million, down 14.9% year over year, as commercial construction activity remained soft and project awards continued to slip. The decline also reflects a pause in new GV-400 orders by three OEM customers pending publication of the recall notice, and we are working with those customers as replacement valve shipments progress. Segment backlog was $343.8 million, roughly flat year over year. In BCV we are managing for cash and contribution, and Project Keystone actions are concentrated where volumes have fallen fastest.

**On the GV-400 recall.** In September we voluntarily initiated a recall of approximately 41,000 GV-400 and GV-410 series combination gas valves sold to OEM customers, working with the CPSC under its Fast Track program, with a parallel notification to Health Canada. In affected units, a diaphragm can deform under sustained high-inlet-pressure conditions and allow gas to pass when the valve is commanded closed. We identified the root cause — a supplier lot of diaphragm compound that was out of specification on compression set following a supplier change in Q1 2025 — completed corrective action, and have been shipping replacement valves from our Mequon plant since 28 September. We recorded a $21.6 million charge in the quarter to reserve field replacement, OEM labor reimbursement and logistics costs, and we have lodged a recovery claim of approximately $9 million against the supplier, which is not recognized in that reserve. The recall notice published in October sets out the affected date codes and the remedy for customers. This was a customer-first decision, and we believe acting quickly was the right call.

## Outlook

We are updating our full-year FY2026 guidance to reflect the softer commercial HVAC market and the GV-400 recall. We now expect net sales of $1.66-1.70 billion, compared with our prior range of $1.78-1.84 billion, and adjusted EBITDA of $205-215 million, compared with $255-270 million previously. The updated ranges include the effect of the paused GV-400 orders at several OEM customers. Project Keystone remains on track: we took $6.2 million of restructuring actions in the quarter ($9.8 million year to date) and continue to target $35 million of annualized run-rate savings by the end of Q2 FY2027, with the majority of the benefit realized in FY2027. Our TDC backlog supports growth into FY2027 as scheduled deliveries convert.

Turning to the balance sheet. As of September 30, 2026, we were not in compliance with the financial maintenance covenants under our credit agreement. We have requested a waiver and amendment from our lenders and are in active discussions with the bank group. We ended the quarter with $96.4 million of cash. Further detail will be included in our Form 10-Q.

## Closing

We want to thank our 6,200 employees — particularly our quality, manufacturing and field teams, who moved quickly to identify and remediate the GV-400 issue, and our TDC organization, which delivered another record backlog quarter. We know the third quarter was a difficult one on the fundamentals, and we are not looking past that. What we can control is execution: completing the recall, converting our data-center backlog, delivering Keystone savings and restoring our financial flexibility. Thank you for your continued support and confidence.

Dana Whitcombe, President & Chief Executive Officer
Mark Ostrander, EVP & Chief Financial Officer

---

Forward-looking statements: This letter contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, including statements regarding our guidance, backlog conversion, cost savings, the GV-400 recall and related costs, and liquidity, covenant, waiver and amendment matters. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied, including as a result of the matters described in this letter. See "Risk Factors" in our Annual Report on Form 10-K filed with the SEC and our Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.

**On the GV-400 recall.** In September we voluntarily initiated a recall of approximately 41,000 GV-400 and GV-410 series combination gas valves sold to OEM customers, working with the CPSC under its Fast Track program, with a parallel notification to Health Canada. In affected units, a diaphragm can deform under sustained high-inlet-pressure conditions and allow gas to pass when the valve is commanded closed. We identified the root cause — a supplier lot of diaphragm compound that was out of specification on compression set following a supplier change in Q1 2025 — completed corrective action, and have been shipping replacement valves from our Mequon plant since 28 September. We recorded a $21.6 million charge in the quarter to reserve field replacement, OEM labor reimbursement and logistics costs, and we have lodged a recovery claim of approximately $9 million against the supplier, which is not recognized in that reserve. The recall notice published in October sets out the affected date codes and the remedy for customers. This was a customer-first decision, and we believe acting quickly was the right call.

## Outlook

We are updating our full-year FY2026 guidance to reflect the softer commercial HVAC market and the GV-400 recall. We now expect net sales of $1.66-1.70 billion, compared with our prior range of $1.78-1.84 billion, and adjusted EBITDA of $205-215 million, compared with $255-270 million previously. The updated ranges include the effect of the paused GV-400 orders at several OEM customers. Project Keystone remains on track: we took $6.2 million of restructuring actions in the quarter ($9.8 million year to date) and continue to target $35 million of annualized run-rate savings by the end of Q2 FY2027, with the majority of the benefit realized in FY2027. Our TDC backlog supports growth into FY2027 as scheduled deliveries convert.
